name: Dientes de Navarino circuit
why: The southernmost trek on Earth: jagged rock teeth, empty lakes and Cape Horn's islands on the horizon.
book: Register with the Carabineros in Puerto Williams before and after. No huts, no services: full camping kit and food for a spare day. Bring stove fuel from Punta Arenas (none in Puerto Williams).
dangers: The route is marked only by cairns: you need a map, GPS and navigation skills.
Snow possible every month; storms off the Southern Ocean.
Steep scree passes (Paso Australia, Paso Ventarrón).
turnaround: Wait out a storm in the forest camps rather than crossing a pass in it.

points.name: Trailhead above Puerto Williams
points.note: The track leaves the road at the end of Puerto Williams, by the Virgin shrine on the way to the waterfall.

points.name: Cerro Bandera, Puerto Williams
points.note: About 1.5 h of steep forest: the Chilean flag at 610 m, the Beagle Channel and Ushuaia's mountains below.

points.name: Laguna del Salto, Navarino
points.note: Night 1: the camp by the first lake, under the first towers.

points.name: Dientes de Navarino over Laguna Escondida
points.note: Night 2: the rock teeth stand straight over the lake; Paso Ventarrón, the windiest pass, comes next.

points.name: Laguna Martillo, Navarino
points.note: Night 3: the long hammer-shaped lake, after Paso Guerrico.

points.name: Bahía Virginia road end
points.note: Down from Paso Virginia to the coast road, 6 km west of Puerto Williams: walk, hitch or book a taxi.
